title: 4-Transistor Ternary Content Addressable Memory Cell Design using Stacked Hybrid IGZO/Si Transistors
problem: TCAM implementations require large cell areas and consume significant power. Traditional 16T SRAM-based TCAMs suffer from poor area efficiency and high energy-delay product, limiting deployment in high-speed search applications.
motivation: Efficient TCAM design is critical for content-based search operations in networking and database systems that require fast associative lookups.
method: A 4-transistor stacked cell (POST-RAM) vertically integrates read and write transistors in a single footprint, using InGaZnO channels for write transistors to achieve long retention and single-crystal silicon for read transistors enabling fast access. A self-clamped searching scheme (SC2S) optimizes TCAM search efficiency. Design is validated via 3D-TCAD simulation.
key_novelty: Hybrid IGZO/Si orthogonally stacked transistor configuration that combines extended memory retention with fast read performance in a 4-transistor cell footprint.
contributions: 4T stacked POST-RAM cell design achieving 6x area reduction
Self-clamped searching scheme for efficient TCAM operations
20% energy-delay product improvement over conventional designs
40% delay improvement compared to 16T SRAM-based TCAM
limitations: Practical deployment challenges and silicon validation are not discussed; analysis is based entirely on 3D-TCAD simulation.
primary_theme: Stacked hybrid transistor TCAM for area and energy optimization
